Subject: Temporary CMK acceptance, SSO operator mapping, and audit export path

Team / Linda,

Following up from last week's commercial call — MediSolve has formally asked for a temporary CMK (customer-managed key) acceptance window to enable a pilot in their staging environment. They also raised questions about how our SSO operator roles map to their identity model, and whether audit exports (raw event log dumps) can be routed to their cloud storage without breaking our retention guarantees.

Quick summary of asks: 
- Temporary CMK acceptance: 48–72 hour window for test keys to be used in staging (they want short-lived CMKs, then rotation back to Redwood-managed).
- SSO operator mapping: MediSolve needs a clear mapping doc for our operator-level roles vs. their IdP groups (read-only operator, ingest/operator, emergency-unseal).
- Audit export path: they want scheduled audit export (daily delta) to their S3 bucket; we need to confirm that does not create retention/replication policy conflicts.

I've attached an initial evidence checklist and a rough routing proposal (route_proposal.drawio) — please review. Goal: come back with a tech decision and a proposed timeline by EOD tomorrow so procurement can prepare an SOW/DocuSign flow.

Proposed meeting: 2026-05-19 16:00 PT (30m) — quick triage if needed.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineering Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: evidence_checklist.xlsx; route_proposal.drawio

On Tue, May 19, 2026 at 08:14 AM Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team / Linda,
>
> Following up from last week's commercial call — MediSolve has formally asked for a temporary CMK...
>
> Proposed meeting: 2026-05-19 16:00 PT (30m) — quick triage if needed.

Short notes from infra/runtime perspective: 
- Temporary CMKs: we can support a short-lived CMK for staging if we treat it as an ephemeral key in front of the KV cache. Important constraints: we must not persist a long-term encrypted cache blob with a key we no longer control. For the 48–72h window that should be fine provided the key's lifecycle is visible to our rotation job. See attached KMS handshake notes (kms_handshake_notes.pdf).
- Audit export: routing daily deltas to external S3 is feasible, but we need to:
  1) ensure exports are immutable once written (use object lock or signed manifests)
  2) avoid writing PII in cleartext — exports must be either redacted or encrypted with the customer's key (if they want to own the key for the export, we can write encrypted blobs to their bucket).
- SSO operator mapping: mapping doc is small — operator roles in Redwood are: operator.read, operator.ingest, operator.emergency_unseal. Priya, we need your product input on whether operator.emergency_unseal requires change to our canary/fallback policies.

Risk notes: temporary CMKs + cache = small window where cached tokens could be decryptable by key holder after rotation. Recommend: 
- Short TTL for any cached artifacts derived from CMK
- Forced KV cache flush (or re-encrypt) right after rotation

I'll be on the 16:00 PT call.

—Karthik 
Karthik Iyer
Director, Infrastructure & Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachment: kms_handshake_notes.pdf
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Linda Zhao <linda.zhao@medisolve.health>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary CMK acceptance, SSO operator mapping, and audit export path

Thanks Ben / Karthik — quick product constraints and suggested acceptance criteria: 
- For a short-lived CMK acceptance we need:
  * explicit scope: staging only (no production tenant binding)
  * automated rollback: if the key isn't rotated back by X hours we auto-disable staging CMK use (safety net)
  * test vector set: must run our standard prompt/eval suite to validate no data leakage in outputs (Marissa, I'll need a short list of evals we can run)
- For SSO operator mapping: we can publish a one-page matrix mapping our operator roles to standard SAML groups. We should include minimum recommended attributes (email, groups, subject).
- Audit export path: product will permit exports for staging if export buckets are pre-registered and we have an exported-manifest checksum in our system. We cannot accept export destinations that prevent us from meeting retention SLAs for production tenant data.

Action items I propose for tomorrow: 
1) Marissa: prepare a 1-page compliance evidence checklist (SOC2 snapshot + sample audit export manifest) — due EOD 19 May.
2) Karthik: confirm the cache-flush / re-encrypt plan and estimated engineering effort (hours) — due EOD 19 May.
3) Ben: coordinate procurement ask and share SOW template if MediSolve wants vendor-managed S3 with object-lock.

I will join the 16:00 PT call but please try to keep it to 20 minutes — we just need decision points.

—Priya
Priya Natarajan
Director, Product (Security & Compliance)
Redwood Inference
From: Linda Zhao <linda.zhao@medisolve.health>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 13:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary CMK acceptance, SSO operator mapping, and audit export path

Ben / team — thanks for the clear breakdown. A few procurement and compliance notes from our side: 
- Procurement: we will need a 30-day SOW draft + DocuSign-ready statement that calls out the pilot window and acceptance criteria. Our procurement team is on copy (procurement@medisolve.health).
- Evidence: SOC2 Type II link (we can accept a time-stamped snapshot), plus an audit manifest example for exports. If you can provide a sample manifest and the checksum process that will help us sign off faster.
- KMS: we cannot accept any process that would allow our private key material to be copied or stored outside our control. If Redwood writes encrypted blobs to our S3 using our public key and never has access to the plaintext key post-rotation, that is acceptable.

We are available for the 16:00 PT call; procurement may drop in at the start.

Thanks,
Linda Zhao
Head of Infrastructure
MediSolve Health

2) Audit export: APPROVED for staging if MediSolve provides a registered bucket and object-lock or encrypted blobs (customer-held key). Marissa to provide sample export manifest + checksum example. Owner: marissa_cole.
3) SSO operator mapping: Priya to draft the one-page mapping doc and recommended attribute set. Owner: priya_natarajan.
4) Procurement/SOW: Ben to send a 30-day pilot SOW draft + DocuSign link by tomorrow morning. Owner: ben_carter.

Open question (low priority): verify that export manifests do not include raw prompt contents in clear — Marissa to confirm redaction status in manifest.

I'll follow up with the SOW and link to the shared Drive folder (evidence + artifacts). Next check-in slated for Mon 24 May for any post-pilot gaps.
